messages.speaker: them
messages.text: been looking at trains for the second weekend of september and honestly the prices have dropped since spring. if we book by thursday it works out about half of what we paid in may

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: seriously? that's the weekend after your work thing, right?

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: right, so i'd come to you friday evening and stay until monday morning. and my manager finally approved the extra day, so i wouldn't be travelling back sunday night in the dark

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: that changes everything. my flat's free that week too, my flatmate is at her sister's

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: oh that's good. two questions though: do you want the quiet version of the plan or the loud one, and how do you feel about an early ferry on the saturday?

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: loud, obviously. and ferries are fine as long as i'm not the one driving after

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: fair. then i'd say saturday markets in the morning, that long walk along the water after lunch, and if the weather holds, the little museum with the ship models. sunday can stay empty on purpose

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: you've basically written an itinerary while i was eating dinner

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: i know. i've been unsupervised in a spreadsheet all afternoon. tell me if there's anything you'd hate — food, hills, crowds — before i get too attached to this

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: crowds after 3pm, no. hills fine. food never an issue

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: noted, that rounds the plan down nicely actually. shall i book the seats tonight, or do you want to check your saturday first?

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: book them. if i get stuck i'll swap, i've done worse

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: booked. two return seats on the quiet side of the carriage, and i checked your platform section so you don't have to cross the whole station. goodnight — confirmation should land tomorrow morning

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: confirmation came through this morning. while i remember — does your building still have that guest parking rule, in case i bring the car instead?

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: no rule anyone actually enforces, but the street fills up after nine

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: then i'd aim early and walk the last stretch. how is the shoulder by the way — you said it was still sore after the move?

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: mostly fine, it complains if i sleep on it wrong. no lifting the giant suitcase

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: it'll be the small one, prague taught me that lesson for good. last practical thing: is your kettle the slow kind or the fast kind? some mornings matter more than others

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: the fast kind, i replaced it after that winter

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: perfect, then we are operationally ready. i'll stop planning now and let september do the work

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: you say that like you believe it

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: i don't. there's a whole notes app of ideas for the sunday you haven't vetoed yet

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: sunday was supposed to be the empty one

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: empty by design, not by accident. i keep one rain standby — the covered market — unless that's too touristy for a local these days?

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: it's touristy but the cheese stall earns it. so yes

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: then sunday is sorted if the weather turns, and the good days get to stay unplanned. those are my favourite ones

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: small detour from the plan: my sister asked if she can borrow the friday, so would you rather i came thursday night, or we shift the whole thing a week?

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: thursday night works, more saturday that way

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: that's what i thought too. one more while we're at it: the big breakfast place — first morning, or keep it for the last one as a send-off?

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: last morning. it's a send-off, not a starter

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: agreed, which conveniently settles another corner of the plan. i'll bring your book back too — i finally finished it the week my flatmate was away

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: and? you never actually told me

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: the middle sags where he over-explains, but the ending is better than i ever gave it credit for. which reminds me — did you fold the corner of page 91 too, or am i unique in my crimes?

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: page 91 is entirely my fault, i was on a train

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: then we are both guilty, and it's exactly the kind of thing to argue about over that breakfast. nearly two weeks to go

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: i'll give the kettle a descale as a treat

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: it has earned it. i'll also pack the tin from the baker near the office unless you've gone off it

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: nobody has ever gone off that tin

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: glad we agree on the essentials. goodnight — next time we talk i'll have a train time and probably three more questions
